# wl sync blocked: inbound worklog commits authored sorra@thewizardscode.com fail the author-identity gate

## Problem statement

`wl sync` in the SorraAgents checkout refuses to merge inbound worklog data when the incoming commits are authored by `sorra@thewizardscode.com` — a genuine project work identity used by the operator's other checkouts — because the author-identity gate accepted only the configured `user.email` (the GitHub noreply identity) plus the earlier `pi@local` exception. Work items and comments written from a `sorra@` checkout therefore stranded on the remote, and local work could not be published either (`wl sync --no-push` failed at the same pull/merge step).

## Users

- **Producer/operator (uses multiple checkouts).** "As the operator, I want worklog changes made from my `sorra@thewizardscode.com` checkout to merge on every agent host, so I do not have to re-author or hand-replay history per batch."
- **Agent sessions (Map, plan, audit).** "As an agent, I want `wl sync` to complete without `--allow-foreign-author`, so intake/plan/audit work is published instead of being stranded behind a gate refusal."

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wl sync` completes in the SorraAgents checkout (pull, merge and push) for inbound commits authored by `sorra@thewizardscode.com`, with no `--allow-foreign-author` override.
- The chosen policy is recorded in `syncAllowedAuthors` (`.worklog/config.yaml`) with a rationale comment, and the allow-list stays exact-email: no wildcards, no allow-all, empty author email still refused.
- The gate still refuses incident sentinel identities (`t@t.com` and the other `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`), and no sentinel is ever added to the allow-list.
- Testing/validation: `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py` passes and continues to pin exact-email semantics, empty-email refusal and sentinel refusal.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Policy-only fix: the gate decision logic is unchanged, so the existing regression contract (`tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`) remains authoritative.
- The allow-list may not be widened beyond an explicit email list — no wildcard, no allow-all, and the empty-author-email refusal is never bypassed.
- Work is pushed to `dev` only (`main` is promoted by the ship skill).

## Existing state (verified during intake, 2026-11-04)

- `.worklog/config.yaml` → `syncAllowedAuthors` contains `250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`, `pi@local` and `sorra@thewizardscode.com`, with a comment recording that the last entry is the project's own work identity, not a sentinel (`4e1ec2b6f`, present on `dev` and `main`).
- `scripts/check_git_identity.py` gate logic unchanged; `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` untouched.
- `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py` drives the real exported `checkAuthorIdentity` gate and pins: `pi@local` accepted only via the allow-list, arbitrary foreign email refused, empty email refused even with `allowForeignAuthor`, sentinels never allow-listed. It reads the real project config, so the added entry participates in its membership/exactness assertions; the entry is not individually pinned by name.
- Verification this session: `wl sync --no-push` merged the inbound worklog data with no author-identity refusal (57 work items updated, 0 comments added, 0 `--allow-foreign-author` usage), so the four previously refused commits (`14e4cc89e`, `273325c35`, `23c315392`, `e8c0011a7`) now merge.
- Recurrence pattern: the same identity was refused on 2026-10-27 and again on 2026-10-29/10-31 (recurrence comment `SA-C0MVWICFTW001KBWQ`).

## Desired change

`sorra@thewizardscode.com` is accepted permanently as a permitted worklog-sync author through the project allow-list, while the gate's exact-email, empty-email and sentinel guarantees stay intact and continue to be covered by the existing regression tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.worklog/config.yaml` — `syncAllowedAuthors` entry plus the rationale comment (landed in `4e1ec2b6f`)
- `scripts/check_git_identity.py` — gate entry point and allow-list contract metadata; decision logic unchanged
- `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py` — allow-list contract regression tests (exact-email, empty-email, sentinel refusal)
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — gate rules and the allow-list remediation procedure

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `sorra@thewizardscode.com` is a real project identity, not a leaked/sentinel identity — it is absent from `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` and the producer explicitly chose to allow-list it rather than re-author history.
- **Risk (drift):** no test pins the individual `sorra@` entry; removing it would re-strand sync, but loudly (a gate refusal on the next sync), and the contract-level guarantees stay pinned — accepted.
- **Risk (scope):** further identities must each be a separately reviewed config change, not bundled into this item.
- **Risk (widening):** the allow-list is a project-wide policy widening; it stays bounded because matching is exact-email and empty emails are always refused.

## Related work

- SA-0MVLJDS04002KI1W — previous occurrence; the considered-but-rejected alternative (re-author the inbound `t@t.com` commits).
- SA-0MVGSB63F00803HK — precedent: allow-listing `pi@local` with the same bounded, exact-email approach.
- SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS — original author-identity gate incident and allow-list remediation guidance.
- SA-0MSW9RF740016WC7 — batch blocked by empty emails / `ross@example.com`.
- SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2 — `t@t.com`-authored commits on `refs/worklog/data`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview round was required: the seed description already contained the problem statement and ACs, and the open decision had been answered by the producer in the worklog record.

- Q: "How should the four inbound `sorra@thewizardscode.com` worklog commits be handled — (1) allow-list the identity, (2) re-author the commits to the configured GitHub identity, or (3) another machine/agent identity policy?" — Answer (producer, plan session `herdr-1793454596-4112787-24238`, 2026-10-31): option 1, add the identity to the allow-list. Source: worklog comment `SA-C0MVWIN02D006Y7YM`. Research: the rejected alternative (re-authoring, the SA-0MVLJDS04002KI1W playbook) would fix this batch only and recur on the next push from a `sorra@` checkout.
- Q: "Is `sorra@thewizardscode.com` a genuine identity or an incident sentinel?" — Answer (agent research): genuine project work identity; it is not listed in `scripts/check_git_identity.py::INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` and the config comment records it as the project's own work identity. Evidence: `.worklog/config.yaml`, `scripts/check_git_identity.py`.
- OPEN QUESTION: none.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSW9RF740016WC7** – wl sync blocked: 117 remote worklog commits fail author-identity gate (empty email / ross@example.com) (completed)
- **SA-0MVLJDS04002KI1W** – wl sync blocked again: inbound t@t.com-authored worklog commits fail the author-identity gate (completed)
- **SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2** – wl sync blocked again: inbound t@t.com-authored worklog commits on refs/worklog/data (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: accept, acceptance, add, agent, allow (+70 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: accept, add, agent, allow, author (+69 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: accept, acceptance, add, agent, allow (+69 more)

## Impact

Operator worklog sync from checkouts using `sorra@thewizardscode.com` now completes without manual intervention or `--allow-foreign-author` overrides.
data.title: wl sync blocked: inbound worklog commits authored sorra@thewizardscode.com fail the author-identity gate

# Driven child sessions do not hold the per-child lock, so the herdr hydrator demotes them mid-implementation

discovered-from:SA-0MVTE927L0017ND5

## Problem statement

A driven child session is pane-less by construction, so the herdr hydrator's
"busy = pane OR live claim holder" rule is the *only* thing keeping its
`in-progress` claim alive — but the per-child `flock` is acquired and released
inside the short-lived `implement.py start` subprocess, so no live `flock`
exists while the driven session actually works. The hydrator therefore sees a
pane-less item with a dead claim holder and demotes it to `open` mid-session,
which both makes the worklog lie and re-opens the item for a second, duplicate
dispatch onto the same worktree.

## Users

- **Producer / operator watching the herdr UI.** Story: *As a producer, I want
  a driven child that is genuinely being implemented to stay `in-progress` in
  the worklog and the herdr UI, so I can trust the board and do not have to
  re-dispatch or rescue an item the hydrator demoted under a working agent.*
- **Driven child session (the implementing agent).** Story: *As a driven child
  session, I want to hold my own per-child lock for my whole lifetime, so the
  hydrator never demotes me mid-work and no second session is handed my
  worktree.*
- **Drive orchestrator (`implement.py drive`).** Story: *As the drive
  orchestrator, I want to own the child's lock for the duration of the spawned
  session and pass the ownership token to that session, so the documented
  "one child = one holder" contract is true for driven (pane-less) children
  too.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1. **Lock is held for the session's whole lifetime.** While a driven child
  session is alive — from the driver's spawn until the session exits —
  `<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock` is held by a live kernel `flock` and the
  lock file's recorded `pid` names a live process. The herdr hydrator's
  existing live-claim-holder rule (`WL-0MVWDB3IG004NRIU`, already implemented
  in ContextHub) therefore sees the item as busy and never demotes it to
  `open`.
- 2. **The spawned session receives the ownership token and re-enters.** The
  driven session receives `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN` matching the lock
  file's token, and its own `implement.py start` / `finish` re-enter the lock
  as a token-based re-entrant no-op instead of being refused as
  `skipped-held`. Ownership stays token-based — never inferred from pid
  equality.
- 3. **Release is bounded to the session.** The lock is released when the
  spawned session exits — on success, non-zero exit and timeout — so no stale
  `flock` survives the session, and the next `parent` / `start` acquires the
  lock cleanly (or reclaims a genuinely dead holder with the existing
  warning + report fields).
- 4. **A different live owner is still refused.** If the lock is already held
  by a *different* live owner when the driver tries to hold it for the
  session, the driver reports `skipped-held` (with `held_by`, `held_children`)
  and spawns no session — the existing duplicate-dispatch protection is not
  weakened.
- 5. **Regression test with a fake spawner.** A test drives `phase_drive`
  with an injectable fake spawner and asserts, from inside the spawner, that
  the lock is held (kernel `flock` live, recorded `pid` live, token present
  in the child environment) for the session's lifetime and released once the
  spawner returns; the existing per-child-lock suites
  (`test_phase_start_child_lock.py`, `test_drive_child_lock.py`,
  `test_drive_child_session.py`) stay green.
- 6. **Documentation updated.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` describe the driven-session
  lock-holder behaviour accurately (who holds the lock, for how long, how the
  token reaches the session, and the failure/timeout release paths).
- 7. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (enforced by the
  dev-push gate).

## Impact

A driven child that is actively being implemented now stays `in-progress` in
the worklog and the herdr UI instead of being silently demoted to `open` four
minutes into its session, so producers can trust the board and no second agent
is dispatched onto the same worktree.

## Constraints

- **Ownership must stay token-based.** `_probe_child_lock` and
  `WorkItemLock` already treat a matching `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN` as a
  re-entrant no-op; the fix must not add a pid-equality ownership heuristic.
- **The recorded `pid` must name a live process.** The hydrator trusts the
  recorded pid only when it is alive and not a reused pid; a lock file whose
  pid is the dead `start` subprocess is exactly the observed bug.
- **The lock must live in `<worklog>/locks/`**, never inside the worktree
  (the worktree can be removed mid-flight).
- **No change to the hydrator.** The ContextHub side is already fixed
  (`WL-0MVWDB3IG004NRIU` / `WL-0MVWDAZL10025P8J`); this item is the producer
  side of that contract.
- **Existing lock semantics preserved:** fail-closed on ambiguous state,
  stale-dead-pid reclamation with a warning, `skipped-held` classification,
  the `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE` recursion guard, and the worktree placement
  guard.
- **Out of scope:** changing the hydrator, changing `--assignee` scheduling
  semantics, or adding a heartbeat/TTL protocol.

## Existing state

- `phase_start` acquires the per-child lock (`_new_child_lock` →
  `WorkItemLock.acquire()`), holds it for the start critical section, and
  releases it in a `finally` (`implement.py:9983`, `implement.py:10062`).
- `phase_drive` runs `parent` (which runs `start` as a subprocess), then
  spawns a fresh Pi session for `next_child` via `_default_session_spawner`
  or `_pane_session_spawner` (`implement.py:15421`, spawn at
  `implement.py:16188`).
- `_child_session_env` propagates `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN` **only when the
  current process already holds a lock or inherits the env token**
  (`implement.py:13081`, `_child_lock_token` at `implement.py:1298`). The
  driver holds no lock while it waits for the session, so the spawned session
  gets no token.
- Measured during the incident: `.worklog/locks/child-<id>.lock` recorded a
  dead pid (the exited `start` subprocess) and `fuser` showed no holders,
  while the driven session was alive and had already written its red test.
- The documented contract already claims the token is exported "to the driven
  child session" and the lock is "held for the holder's lifetime"
  (`skill/implement/SKILL.md:1078-1102`,
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md:2290-2306`); the drive path does not
  meet it.

## Desired change

Make the driven session's per-child lock live for the session's whole
lifetime. **Recommended approach (A):** the long-lived driver (`phase_drive`)
acquires the child's `WorkItemLock` immediately before spawning the session,
keeps it held while the spawner waits for the session, and releases it in a
`finally` after the session exits; it propagates the lock's token to the
spawned session (and to the `parent`/`start`/`finish` subprocesses it invokes)
so they re-enter rather than block. The lock file's recorded pid is then the
live driver pid.

Alternative considered **(B):** have the driven session itself hold the
`flock` for its lifetime. Rejected as the default because the session's
`start`/`finish` are short-lived subprocesses and the Pi agent process does
not hold file descriptors for a lock; option B would need a dedicated
long-lived lock-holder process in the session (more moving parts than
option A). The item's stated direction permits either, and the chosen
approach must still satisfy all ACs above.

Either way: the lock-file `pid` must name a live process, and
`_probe_child_lock` must stay token-based.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` (acquire/hold/release
  the child lock around the spawn), `_child_session_env` (propagate the held
  lock's token explicitly), `_child_lock_token` / `_new_child_lock` (token
  plumbing), possibly a small helper to hold the lock across the spawn.
- `skill/shared/work_item_lock.py` — only if a re-entrancy or explicit-token
  seam is needed; the primitive itself should stay unchanged.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_child_lock.py` — extend the
  drive-side lock coverage; keep existing re-entrancy tests green.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py` — fake-spawner test for
  the session-lifetime hold (AC5).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_lock.py` — ensure the real
  subprocess two-holder race still passes.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` —
  document the driven-session lock holder.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTE927L0017ND5` — *implement.py finish deletes a plain leaf session's
  cwd…* (the `discovered-from` parent of this item).
- `SA-0MVOABYW00004978` — *Prevent duplicate drive child sessions (exclusive
  per-child lock)* (introduced the lock).
- `SA-0MVQ5AXLF002PAQ3` — *Implement: acquire lock in phase_start +
  skipped-held* (wired the lock into `phase_start`).
- `SA-0MVQ7VMRL00498YB` — the per-child lock reference section
  (`docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`).
- ContextHub `WL-0MVW9UQQ6004KSXY` — *hydrator demotes in-progress claims of
  pane-less driven sessions* (parent bug); children `WL-0MVWDAZL10025P8J`
  (claim-holder probe), `WL-0MVWDB3IG004NRIU` (busy = pane OR live claim
  holder), `WL-0MVWDB7F2003SORI` (release clears the scheduling hold) — all
  done; they assume the producer-side lock is actually held.
- `SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9` — the "actively worked ⇒ in_progress" invariant.
- `SA-0MVL7YG2S009L6PU` — *wl sync: file-lock age-expiry steals a live
  holder's lock* (a different lock — the ContextHub `wl sync` file lock — but
  the same "a live holder must never be treated as dead" principle).

## Risks

- **Driver death while the session lives (option A).** If the driver is killed
  while a spawned session is still working, the kernel releases the driver's
  `flock` and the hydrator may demote the item even though the session is
  alive. Mitigation: the driver is normally the long-lived process that waits
  for the session; document the residual window. Option B (session-held lock)
  would close it but needs a dedicated lock-holder process.
- **Stale token reuse across children.** A driver that holds child A's token
  and then acquires child B's lock must generate a fresh token for B, not
  inherit A's, or `_probe_child_lock` could misclassify B as self-owned.
  Mitigation: acquire each child's lock with a fresh token and clear/replace
  the env token between iterations.
- **Double-acquire ordering.** `phase_drive` runs `parent` (which runs
  `start`, acquiring and releasing the lock) before spawning the session; the
  driver's own acquire must not collide with a still-held `start` lock.
  Mitigation: acquire only after `parent` returns `next_child` and the
  worktree exists; treat a failed acquire as `skipped-held`.
- **Scope creep.** Adjacent improvements (closing the `start`→driver acquire
  race, hydrator changes, heartbeat) are recorded as separate work items, not
  folded into this fix.

## Assumptions

- **A1:** The recommended fix is option A (the driver holds the lock for the
  spawned session's lifetime and propagates the token). This is a design
  choice; the item permits either option, and the implementer may switch to
  option B if planning finds a concrete blocker, provided all ACs still hold.
- **A2:** The hydrator side is already fixed in ContextHub, so no ContextHub
  change is needed in this item; the AC1 hydrator outcome is a consequence of
  the producer-side lock being held and is covered by ContextHub's existing
  tests.
- **A3:** The driver releases the lock after the spawner returns, before the
  next `parent` iteration, so `parent`/`start`/`finish` acquire a free lock
  (or re-enter by token if invoked while the driver holds it).
- **A4:** The small race between `parent`'s `start` releasing the lock and the
  driver acquiring it for the session is accepted (the worktree already
  exists, so a slipped-in second driver resumes rather than duplicates it);
  closing it entirely is out of scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required. The seed context (observed incident,
root cause with evidence, impact, desired fix direction and proposed ACs) was
sufficient to draft this brief; the only design ambiguity — driver-held versus
session-held lock — is recorded as Assumption A1 with a recommendation, not a
blocking question.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVQ7VMRL00498YB** – Document child lock and held-child diagnosis (completed)
- **SA-0MVQ5AXLF002PAQ3** – Implement: acquire lock in phase_start + skipped-held (completed)
- **SA-0MVQ5AE7L005M0NR** – Implement: shared per-work-item flock lock (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mvoabyw00004978, 0mvq5axlf002paq3, ac1, ac5, acceptance (+340 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac1, ac5, acceptance, accepted, acquire (+338 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mvoabyw00004978, 0mvq7vmrl00498yb, ac1, ac5, accepted (+324 more)
data.title: Driven child sessions do not hold the per-child lock, so the herdr hydrator demotes them mid-implementation

# ship: CHANGELOG release section is discarded by the dev→main merge conflict resolution

**Origin:** observed in the `1916: The Rising` v0.1.23 release (RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L). The Discord release notification went out with no release focus and no changelog body, and `main`'s `CHANGELOG.md` had no `## v0.1.23` section.

## Root cause

In `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` the CHANGELOG is generated **before** `origin/dev` is merged:

1. `generate-changelog.js "$NEW_VERSION"` writes `## v0.1.23 (…)` (with the `> **Release focus:** …` marker) and commits it on the release branch, which is based on `main`.
2. `git merge --no-ff origin/dev` then conflicts on `CHANGELOG.md`, because `dev` carries its own `## Unreleased` block.
3. The auto-resolution runs `git checkout --theirs CHANGELOG.md` — taking dev's whole file and **discarding the generated release section**.
4. The merged tree is tagged, so the released tree carries no `## v<version>` section.

The comment above the resolution (lines 217-219) even claims "generate-changelog.js rewrites it for the new version **afterwards**", contradicting the actual order.

Downstream effects:
- `discord-notify.js` `extractChangelogSection()` returns `null` and `extractReleaseFocus()` finds no marker, so the embed loses both the focus and the release notes (silently — only a focus warning is logged).
- Release notes are absent from `main`/`dev` for that version (recoverable only from the discarded commit).

## Proposed fix

1. Preserve the generated section across the merge: when `CHANGELOG.md` conflicts, take dev's version and then **re-insert** the generated `## v<version>` section (a small, tested helper), instead of discarding it.
2. Assert after the merge that a generated section is still present; abort the release (before tagging) if it was lost. A *failed generation* keeps today's non-fatal behaviour (warn and continue) — this only guards the regression where a successfully generated section is dropped.
3. `discord-notify.js`: log an explicit warning naming the version when no `## v<version>` section is found (still non-blocking).
4. Document the guarantee in `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/changelog-merge.js` (new helper)
- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js`
- `skill/ship/tests/test_changelog_merge.mjs` (new)
- `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs`
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`

## Acceptance criteria

1. With dev's `CHANGELOG.md` modified (an `## Unreleased` block present), the merge-resolution path yields a file that contains the generated `## v<version>` section with its `> **Release focus:**` marker **and** keeps dev's content — asserted by a node test over the new merge helper using a dev-style file.
2. When a section was generated but is missing after the merge, the release script aborts before tagging with an actionable message (non-zero exit) — asserted by a test of the resolution helper's "section lost" outcome plus the script-level guard.
3. A failed generation keeps the non-fatal contract: the release continues with an explicit warning, and the guard does not fire for a section that was never generated — asserted by a test.
4. `discord-notify.js` emits an explicit warning naming the version when the `## v<version>` section is absent, and still sends the notification (non-blocking) — unit test with an injected fetch.
5. The Discord embed still carries both the release focus and the changelog body when a generated section is present — unit test on the composition path.
6. `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` documents the ordering/preservation guarantee and the abort-on-loss behaviour.

## Impact

Every release now keeps its generated `## v<version>` changelog section — including the release focus marker — through the dev→main merge, so released trees and Discord notifications always carry the release notes instead of shipping with no `## v<version>` heading, no focus and no changelog body; a release also aborts before tagging rather than silently shipping without its release notes.
data.title: ship: CHANGELOG release section discarded by the dev→main merge conflict resolution

# audit skill: AC extraction rejects qualified `Acceptance Criteria` headings

**Symptom (observed auditing RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L, 2026-11-01):** `audit_runner.py issue` returned `Ready to close: No` with `No acceptance criteria defined.` and **0 model calls**, then demoted the item to `open`/`plan_complete` — even though the item's description carries three numbered acceptance criteria under the heading `## Acceptance criteria for this project`.

## Root cause

`_extract_acs()` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` matches the AC heading with an anchored regex:

```
^(?:Acceptance|Success)\s+Criteria:?\s*(?:\([^)]*\))?\s*$
```

The match is applied to the line **after** `_normalize_heading_line()` strips markdown heading markers — but a trailing qualifier such as `for this project` is not allowed (only an optional colon or parenthetical is), so the heading never matches and the function returns the `["No acceptance criteria defined."]` sentinel. The pipeline then treats that sentinel as the AC body (a `warning` verdict), skips Phase 2, and produces a `No` verdict which demotes the item.

## Consequences

- A valid, auditable item audits as if it has no ACs: Phase 1 and Phase 2 screening are skipped (0 pi calls), and the item is demoted to `open`/`plan_complete` on the normal `No` path.
- The failure is silent to the model — no prompt ever sees the AC list, so no evidence names the extraction failure.

## Reproduction

`audit_runner.py issue` against an item whose description AC-section heading carries a trailing qualifier, e.g. `## Acceptance criteria for this project` (RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L exhibited this; its three criteria were manually verified satisfied, and the heading had to be normalised to `## Acceptance Criteria` before the audit would screen them).

## Suggested fix

Relax the heading pattern to accept trailing free text while keeping canonical headings byte-compatible: e.g. match `Acceptance Criteria` / `Success Criteria` optionally followed by `:`, a parenthetical, a trailing qualifier (`for …`), or end-of-line. Add regression tests covering heading variants: canonical, lowercase `c`, colon, parenthetical, and a trailing-qualifier heading.

### Reuse note (plan review)

The shared extractor `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` already matches AC headings on a **prefix** basis (`^#+\s+Acceptance\s+Criteria`, case-insensitive), so it already accepts a trailing qualifier. Do not build a second, divergent matcher: keep the relaxed audit pattern semantically aligned with that prefix match so the audit pipeline and the plan/tree-coverage pipeline agree on what is an AC section.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `_extract_acs()` (or the heading matcher it uses) recognises AC headings with a trailing qualifier (e.g. `## Acceptance criteria for this project`), extracting the numbered/bulleted items below them.
2. Canonical headings (`## Acceptance Criteria`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Success Criteria`, optional colon/parenthetical) behave unchanged — no regression.
3. A unit test covers the exact qualifier variant from the RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L reproduction.

## Impact

Items whose AC heading carries a short qualifier now get genuinely screened by the audit instead of silently auditing as having no acceptance criteria and being demoted back to planning.

data.description:
# audit: gap-mapped children re-screen in-main-slot and overwrite serviced child audits

## Observed on SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB (epic, all 10 children terminal and on dev)

An epic audit whose **parent** carries one `partial` AC cannot converge while the
default in-main-slot child-audit mode is active. Every run re-screens the same
gap-mapped children, re-blocks on the pending-screens gate, and (worse) overwrites
child audits that a previous session had serviced with real verdicts.

## Root cause (two interacting behaviours)

1. **Gap-mapped children ignore their stored verdict.** In the default
   parent-first flow (`_phase_children`, `audit_children=False`) the
   `not parent_gaps` branch consults `_child_content_changed()` (content-gated
   reuse), but the `elif child["id"] in gap_child_ids:` branch appends the child
   to `pending_children` **without** consulting its stored audit — unlike the
   `--audit-children` P7 pre-pass, which reuses a fresh stored child audit via
   `_get_child_audit_verdict()` and never re-screens it.
2. **In-main-slot mode cannot service screens inside the run.** With
   `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` (default `true`) the gap-mapped child screens are
   emitted as `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` and the child audits are persisted as
   `partial` + `main-session review`. A later `persist` pass then **overwrites**
   the previously serviced, evidence-backed child audit with that pending
   `partial` report.

Net effect: service the screens → re-run the parent → the children are re-screened
and their good audits are destroyed → the parent still reports
`Ready to close: No` with `Child screens pending`. The
`<id>.pending-screens.json` signal is never cleared.

## Evidence (this item's run)

| Step | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Audit run 1 | 08:13 | `Ready to close: No`, 7 in-main-slot screens emitted |
| Screens serviced by the session (real file:line evidence) | ~09:55 | 6 children `Yes`, 1 `No` (documented downstream AC) |
| Audit re-run (`--force`, because the stored report was content-fresh) | 10:04 | 14 screens re-emitted; **all 7 child audits overwritten back to `partial` + `main-session review`**; parent `No` with 7 pending screens |
| Screens re-serviced by hand (again) | 10:20 | 6 `Yes` / 1 `No` restored |

The parent's single blocking AC (SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB AC10) is a downstream
verification owned by a **different repository** (`LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X`), so it can
never become `met` on this host — the loop is permanent, not a transient state.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Reuse before re-screen.** In the default parent-first flow, a
  gap-mapped child with a content-fresh stored audit is reused (its persisted AC
  verdicts adopted, exactly as the `--audit-children` pre-pass does) and is NOT
  added to `pending_children`.
- **AC2 — Serviced audits are never overwritten.** A parent run never persists a
  pending-`partial` child report over a child audit that is content-fresh and
  carries real (non-pending) verdicts.
- **AC3 — Convergence.** With all children terminal and only one unsatisfiable
  parent AC, a re-run after servicing the child screens reports
  `Ready to close: No` naming **that AC only** (no `Child screens pending` gate),
  and the pending-screens signal is cleared.
- **AC4 — Regression tests** cover both flows (gap-mapped reuse, no overwrite on
  persist) with no real `pi` or `audit_runner` subprocess.

## Related work

- SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB — the epic whose audit exposed this (discovered-from).
- SA-0MVAWFUU0004VW45 / SA-0MVAWFYZE0040SQ3 — unserviced in-main-slot handling
  (mitigates the reporting side only; it does not stop the re-screen/overwrite).
- LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X — the cross-repo consumer AC that makes the parent
  permanently `partial` on this host.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** – Audit: parent-first child pass-through (audit parent only first) (completed)
- **SA-0MW2J7O3D0044SFM** – Re-resolve pending children on checkpoint resume (completed)
- **SA-0MU32TE120012T49** – R5: Enforce the child-audit execution contract (no silent pending child screens) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mvawfuu0004vw45, 0mvawfyze0040sq3, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+139 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mvawfuu0004vw45, 0mvawfyze0040sq3, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+133 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+129 more)

data.description:
## Problem

Every `audit_runner.py issue <id>` run that finds a medium/low code-quality finding it classifies as a *candidate false positive*:

1. creates a **new** chore work item (`ruff BLE001 in .../implement.py — candidate false positive — producer decision required`), and
2. sets `needsProducerReview = true` on the audited parent item.

Observed during the 2026-11-02 release prep: a backlog of 20+ such chore items accumulated (SA-0MVBD5ZBD007HQZA, SA-0MVI2ZZH9004WGIG, SA-0MVZIKFES006HD99, SA-0MVZK9SBF000HLS2, SA-0MVZL5TE1007YTVJ, SA-0MVZL69QA0007CRJ, ...), and **7 of 36 in_review items** were blocked by the ship skill's producer-review gate purely because of them. Clearing the flag is a manual `wl update` per item and the next audit re-creates another chore + flag, so a release can never converge.

## Expected

- A false-positive candidate should be recorded **once** (deduplicated by rule + file + line + fingerprint), not once per audit run.
- A passing audit verdict (`readyToClose === true`) should clear / not set `needsProducerReview`; the flag should reflect a genuine producer decision, not the existence of an unresolved low-severity lint candidate.
- Consider a documented producer-level suppression (e.g. a per-rule/file allowlist, or an `auditWaiver`) so accepted false positives stop re-surfacing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Repeated audits of the same unchanged item do not create duplicate chore items (dedupe proven by a test).
2. An audit that ends `Ready to close: Yes` leaves `needsProducerReview` false.
3. An accepted false positive can be recorded once (suppression/waiver) and no longer re-flags the parent.
4. Release gate regression test: a repository with N accepted false-positive chores does not fail the ship producer-review gate.
5. Full suite green.

## Impact

Blocks `/skill:ship release` on repositories with deliberate lint patterns; each release needs manual flag clearing (2026-11-02 release: 7 items cleared by hand).
data.title: audit_runner sets needsProducerReview for every medium/low 'candidate false positive' chore, blocking releases

## Problem

`tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` (added in v0.1.25) builds a fixture release repo and drives `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` with a stubbed suite runner. Under a clean shell the module is green (verified: `run_tests.py --scope full --force` at tree a9b008ead → 5820 passed). Under the **pre-push hook** (i.e. any push to `dev`/`main`) the same three tests fail:

```
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestGreenGate::test_green_gate_invokes_full_scope_and_release_proceeds
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestRedGate::test_red_gate_blocks_release_before_pr
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestMissingRunnerFailClosed::test_missing_runner_fails_closed
FileNotFoundError: .../runner-marker.txt   (the stubbed runner was never invoked)
```

Root cause: git exports `GIT_DIR` (and the suite gate may export `GIT_INDEX_FILE`) into hook environments; the fixture repo's git commands then resolve against the *live* checkout instead of the fixture, so `merge-dev-to-main.sh` short-circuits and the suite gate never runs. This is the same class as SA-0MVYS34QF000AWQX (node fixtures inheriting the finish gate's `GIT_INDEX_FILE`).

**Consequence:** the pre-push full-suite gate is red for every `dev` push, so `dev` cannot be synced with `main` after a release (hit during the 2026-11-02 v0.1.25 release; the sync required `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` with a separately verified green tree).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` scrubs the ambient git environment (`shared.git_sandbox.fixture_git_env()` or equivalent) for both the fixture repo construction and the merge-script subprocess, so it passes when run from a git hook.
2. A regression test proves the module passes with `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_INDEX_FILE` set to the live repository.
3. `git push origin dev` (fast-forward) succeeds without `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` after the fix.
4. Full suite green in both a clean shell and a hook-like environment.

## Related

- SA-0MVYS34QF000AWQX — same leak class for node fixtures.
- SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42 — audit/producer-review churn (unrelated, same release session).
data.title: tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py is not hermetic: fails under the pre-push hook's exported GIT_DIR, blocking dev pushes

## Goal

Prove, with tests, that a run's `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY` describes the current attempt and
that a leftover abort-recovery state file cannot short-circuit or distort a retry.

**User story:** As an operator debugging a failed audit, I want the reliability summary and the
failure evidence to belong to the attempt I just ran, so I am never misled by a previous run's
numbers or by stale recovery state.

## Context / evidence (from the parent plan investigation)

- `_rel_reset()` runs at the top of `cmd_issue` and the summary is emitted once per process, so
  the runner does not replay counters; the "byte-identical" observation is explained by the new
  report never being persisted (Defect 2), leaving the previous run's stored report visible.
- `audit_runner.py` only writes/removes `.audit_state_<id>.json`; it never reads it
  (`check-audit-gate.js` reads it after exit to restore status). A stale state file cannot
  short-circuit a retry today.

## Scope

- Tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_reliability_summary.py` and
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_abort_recovery.py`:
  (a) two sequential `cmd_issue`-equivalent runs with different outcomes produce *different*
  counters and summary values (no bleed-through between runs);
  (b) a pre-existing `.audit_state_<id>.json` (and a stale debug JSONL) present before a run has
  no effect on the verdict, the counters or the retry path, and is cleaned up as today;
  (c) the emitted summary reflects only calls made in this attempt (calls/parse_ok/
  provider_errors/timeouts/verdict_reasks).
- Assert the line remains greppable with the documented stable key order
  (`RELIABILITY_SUMMARY_KEYS` + `elapsed_seconds`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — Tests prove per-run isolation of the reliability counters and the emitted summary line.
- AC2 — A test proves a stale abort-recovery state file present before the run cannot change
  the verdict, counters or retry behaviour (documents current behaviour if no code change is
  needed).
- AC3 — The summary line keeps its stable key set/order and one-emission-per-run contract.
- AC4 — `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/test_audit_reliability_summary.py
  skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_abort_recovery.py` passes.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_reliability_summary.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_abort_recovery.py`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`

## Problem statement

The tracked `.pi-config/agent/models.json` MunitoAI provider lists only `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`. The MunitoAI API serves two DeepSeek models, and the operator wants the newer `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` also available.

## Goal

Implement the failure classification and relatedness helper functions in `audit_runner.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_classify_test_failure_scope(failure)` returns `"unit"` or `"integration"`:
   - Path convention: `tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` → `integration`
   - Everything else → `unit`
   - Unclassifiable (no path data) → `integration` (fail closed)

2. `_failure_relatedness(failure, touched_files, key_files, project_root)` returns `"affected"`, `"unrelated"`, or `"inconclusive"`:
   - Test file path ∈ changed files → `affected`
   - Module imported by test file ∈ changed files → `affected`
   - Changed file is shared test infrastructure (`conftest.py`, `tests/helpers/**`) → `affected`
   - No match → `inconclusive`

3. `_baseline_unrelated(failures, project_root, baseline_commit)` returns per-failure verdicts:
   - Creates scratch worktree at baseline commit (pre-change commit)
   - Runs only inconclusive failures through `paced_runner()` under `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` stand-down
   - Identical failure → `unrelated`; Pass → `affected`
   - Any baseline failure → `affected` (fail closed)
   - Any baseline error (worktree add, merge-base unresolvable, test absent) → `affected` (fail closed, no crash)
   - Never executes the main checkout; never recurses into nested suite runs

4. Scope classification and relatedness algorithm: failures are classified by path convention (`tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` ⇒ integration/end-to-end; everything else ⇒ unit; unclassifiable ⇒ integration, fail closed). Relatedness is decided by deterministic mapping first (failing test file ∈ item's changed files; a module the test imports ∈ changed files; a changed shared test-infrastructure file such as `conftest.py`/`tests/helpers/**`), then — only for inconclusive failures — by a baseline re-run of just those failures in a scratch worktree at the item's pre-change commit (fails identically ⇒ unrelated; passes ⇒ affected). Unit tests cover the pattern table, the import-mapping step, and the baseline comparison (both outcomes), with no real suite execution.

5. No real suite execution in unit tests (mock `paced_runner` / subprocess)
6. Unit tests pass (see child test items)

## Deliverables
- `_classify_test_failure_scope()` — path-pattern classifier
- `_failure_relatedness()` — deterministic mapping + import scan
- `_baseline_unrelated()` — scratch worktree baseline re-run
- Error handling: never crashes, always returns `affected` for infrastructure failures

## Key Files
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (new functions)
